title: Ars Electronica Festival Alles Immer Offen
description: Alles Immer Offen' (Everything Always Open) is a collaborative project within the Ars Electronica Festival framework, emphasizing open-source culture, accessibility, and community-driven artistic practices. The project explores how digital tools and open platforms can democratize creative expression. As Sound Artist and Sound Editor for this 2025 project, he designed immersive soundscapes and edited audio content that enhanced the interactive elements of the installation, creating an auditory experience that complemented the project's themes of openness and digital accessibility.

title: Ars Electronica Festival Campus Exhibition
description: Ars Electronica is an important festival for art, technology, and society, held annually in Linz. The Campus Exhibition showcases projects from universities all around the world, exploring themes of digital innovation and interactive media. In the 2025 festival, he served dual roles as both exhibiting artist and production coordinator, presenting his interactive sound installation 'Embracing Sphere' while managing technical coordination and exhibition logistics for multiple student projects. 'Embracing Sphere' is an immersive audio installation that creates a spatial sound environment where visitors can interact with spatial audio through an audio-tactile seat. The installation utilizes binaural sound mixing and voice coil actuators (bass shakers) to convey an audio-tactile story that reacts to human presence, creating an intimate dialogue between the participant and the sonic environment. The work explores themes of panic and acceptance, drawing inspiration from the renowned film Blade Runner and the mythical place called Tannhäuser Gate.

title: Rundgang Post-Human Resources
description: Rundgang' is the annual graduation exhibition at the University of Art and Design Linz, showcasing student works from various departments. The 'Post-Human Resources' theme explores the intersection of technology, humanity, and artistic expression in contemporary digital culture. As Production Assistant for Rundgang 2025, he contributed to the technical setup, coordination of exhibition spaces, and support for interactive media installations throughout the event.

title: Ars Electronica Festival Sound Campus 'Sonic Fever' Audio Walk
description: The audio walk was developed during the course 'Wave Forms Words,' coordinated by Andreea Vladut. Structured in three parts, with a focus on memory and counter-narrative perspectives, the audio walk will present an altered environment where the gaze shifts to more-than-human agencies and history is presented through a shared collective view. The city will be perceived collectively, offering alternative perspectives on seeing and understanding the city—a city that is re-appropriated and reclaimed by collective voices. Artists: AmiRali Bashiri, Çağla Gillis, I-ID, Mehmet Çolak, Milena Stępień, Sashe Urdovski

title: IC Bright Night
description: IC Bright Night was an experimental electronic music event at ABPU Sonic Lab in Linz, showcasing interactive audiovisual projects from Andreas Weixler's Interface Cultures class, featuring live coding, real-time sound synthesis. With the Sonic Lab's 24-speaker surround system, the program included a playful reimagining of Stockhausen's Helicopter Quartet. Performed by Andrea Corrardi, Ahmed Jamal, Till Schönwetter, Volkan Dinçer, and him. The piece unfolded in a multiplayer game where four virtual helicopter pilots controlled flight, while he directed the spatialized sound with game inputs.

title: Games for Change Turkiye
description: At Games for Change Türkiye Festival 2025, Mehmet Çolak from Serin Sound took the stage with his project “Embracing Sphere.” He explored how multi-sensory environmental storytelling can be conveyed through non-visual audio-tactile mediums, presenting an innovative interaction model blending sound and tactile feedback. Using Embracing Sphere, Çolak demonstrated how interactive audio-tactile interfaces can communicate space, atmosphere, and emotion through sensory perception. Unlike traditional storytelling based on dialogue or cutscenes, environmental storytelling positions the environment as a silent narrator, enabling participants to uncover the narrative through exploration.
